s1.syndrome_frame: liver mass with possible metastasis in a patient with history of colon cancer
salient_findings: 25 mm lesion in segment 8 of the liver
liver tumor with solid and cystic components
absence of the right portal vein and perfusion defect suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
key_facts: 55-year-old man
history of right hemicolectomy for adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon
staged as IIIB (T4N1M0)
no thrombophilic disorders
normal preoperative CEA and CA19-9 levels
completed six months of adjuvant chemotherapy
13 months after surgery, follow-up CT revealed a liver lesion
hepatitis B and C serologies were negative
tumor markers including CEA, CA19-9, α-fetoprotein, and PIVKA-II were within normal limits
liver tumor with two components: solid and cystic
absence of the right portal vein and perfusion defect suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus
no communication with the biliary tree on endoscopic retrograde cholangiography
bile cytology was negative for malignancy

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of colon cancer and liver lesion with characteristics suggestive of metastasis

shortlist.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver tumor with solid and cystic components, although less likely given normal tumor markers

shortlist.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Liver mass with possible biliary involvement, although no communication with the biliary tree was found

shortlist.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Cystic component of the liver tumor, although rare and less likely

shortlist.label: Hepatic adenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign liver tumor, although less likely given the patient's history of colon cancer

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon, and the liver lesion was found 13 months after surgery, which is a common timeframe for metastasis to occur. The presence of a solid and cystic component in the liver tumor and the absence of the right portal vein with a perfusion defect suggestive of portal vein tumor thrombus also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: Normal tumor markers including α-fetoprotein and PIVKA-II make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: No communication with the biliary tree on endoscopic retrograde cholangiography and negative bile cytology for malignancy make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The solid component of the liver tumor and the absence of the right portal vein with a perfusion defect are not typical for this diagnosis

rejected.label: Hepatic adenoma
rejected.why: The patient's history of adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon and the presence of a portal vein tumor thrombus make this benign diagnosis unlikely
